title: Enzymes and genes of taurine and isethionate dissimilation in Paracoccus denitrificans

sections.abstract: <jats:p>Growth of the<jats:italic>α</jats:italic>-proteobacterium<jats:italic>Paracoccus denitrificans</jats:italic>NKNIS with taurine or isethionate as sole source of carbon involves sulfoacetaldehyde acetyltransferase (Xsc), which is presumably encoded by an<jats:italic>xsc</jats:italic>gene in subgroup 3, none of whose gene products has been characterized. The genome of the<jats:italic>α</jats:italic>-proteobacterium<jats:italic>Rhodobacter sphaeroides</jats:italic>2.4.1 was interpreted to contain a nine-gene cluster encoding the inducible dissimilation of taurine, and this deduced pathway included a regulator, a tripartite ATP-independent transporter, taurine dehydrogenase (TDH; presumably TauXY) as well as Xsc (subgroup 3), a hypothetical protein and phosphate acetyltransferase (Pta). A similar cluster was found in<jats:italic>P. denitrificans</jats:italic>NKNIS, in contrast to an analogous cluster encoding an ATP-binding cassette transporter in<jats:italic>Paracoccus pantotrophus</jats:italic>. Inducible TDH, Xsc and Pta were found in extracts of taurine-grown cells of strain NKNIS. TDH oxidized taurine to sulfoacetaldehyde and ammonium ion with cytochrome<jats:italic>c</jats:italic>as electron acceptor. Whereas Xsc and Pta were soluble enzymes, TDH was located in the particulate fraction, where inducible proteins with the expected masses of TauXY (14 and 50 kDa, respectively) were detected by SDS-PAGE. Xsc and Pta were separated by anion-exchange chromatography. Xsc was effectively pure; the molecular mass of the subunit (64 kDa) and the N-terminal amino acid sequence confirmed the identification of the<jats:italic>xsc</jats:italic>gene. Inducible isethionate dehydrogenase (IDH), Xsc and Pta were assayed in extracts of isethionate-grown cells of strain NKNIS. IDH was located in the particulate fraction, oxidized isethionate to sulfoacetaldehyde with cytochrome<jats:italic>c</jats:italic>as electron acceptor and correlated with the expression of a 62 kDa protein. Strain NKNIS excreted sulfite and sulfate during growth with a sulfonate and no sulfite dehydrogenase was detected. There is considerable biochemical, genetic and regulatory complexity in the degradation of these simple molecules.</jats:p>
